Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: SIX CEL animation sheet for Hanni, with a lively but continuous cyclic action.
Use the attached original Hanni as exact character reference: same expressive brown eyes, chibi face/body proportions, orange-red plush fur, cream muzzle and tail tip, dark-brown paws and ear tips, cream/red/gold Hanfu, sash, pendant 汉. Book, when present, is red with exactly “HanNi” and gold plum blossom.
IMPORTANT CANVAS: SQUARE 1:1 overall, exactly THREE columns and TWO rows across this square. Each cell is a tall portrait rectangle. Exactly six full-body cels, ordered left to right/top to bottom. Generous transparent padding, each entire fox and its props inside its own cell.
TRUE TRANSPARENT BACKGROUND. No colored backdrop, no red/brown studio background, no floor, no cast shadows, no glow, no grid, no borders, no gutter lines, no labels, no text beyond HanNi and 汉.
All six are the SAME character with fixed camera, scale, perspective and costume details. Exactly two arms, two paws, two feet, one tail in EVERY cell. Every paw must connect to one sleeve. Never mirror or switch hands. One hand holds its assigned object in all six; the other does the action.
Motion should be clearly readable at 128px: real joint movement of about 10–15 degrees, head nod/tilt up to 3 degrees, tail follow-through, sleeves following the limb. A coherent six-phase loop, not six independent emotional pictures. Phase 6 approaches phase 1 with a similarly small transition as other neighbors; no return-to-rest jump. Same body position and grounded feet except specified hop. No large perspective or character-shape changes. No motion blur.
IDLE. Both paws hug book, gentle closed-mouth smile. 1 relaxed eyes open, tail neutral; 2 chest rises and eyelids lower halfway, tail swings a little left; 3 natural full blink, slight ear twitch; 4 eyes reopen halfway as chest settles, tail returns through center; 5 eyes open glancing a little right, head tilts 2 degrees, tail swings right; 6 gaze and head return almost center, tail begins moving back toward neutral. Calm continuous breathing cycle, not frozen. Body scale and both book paws fixed.
